dangerous_cpts.main_problem: This CPT has multiple distinct failure-associated parameters, all selecting Network_Manipulation=Yes, with strong failure dominance and very little success overlap. Because it is an intermediate diagnostic node directly feeding Root_Causes, and because the repeated failure patterns include several downstream misclassifications involving FDI/System_Fault decisions under different Network_Manipulation columns, there is independent evidence that this CPT may be over-asserting manipulation in some parent configurations.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This is the strongest single parameter in the CPT by failure count, with high confidence and minimal success overlap. In domain terms, when both packet inconsistency patterns are found, the model may be too ready to conclude manipulation, which can propagate to attack-oriented root-cause predictions.

This parameter appears only in failures and never in successes. Although the probability is moderate rather than extreme, its clean failure association suggests this parent configuration may still be biased toward manipulation more often than warranted.

This parameter is also failure-dominant and relatively strong probabilistically. Its recurrence across failure patterns indicates that one-sided evidence from GPTN_1/GPTN_2 may be converted into manipulation too aggressively.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: This CPT is the final decision layer and shows several failure-associated output parameters, especially repeated selection of FDI and one repeated selection of System_Fault under specific upstream combinations. The failure patterns repeatedly terminate at these root-cause columns, and the errors cannot be fully explained by one upstream CPT alone because different upstream activation combinations converge to problematic final labels. That gives this CPT independent plausibility as a contributor to repeated incorrect predictions.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This parameter appears only in failures. Even though 0.55 is not extreme, as an argmax at the final diagnosis node it can systematically tip cases toward FDI. Domain-wise, moderate evidence combinations should not repeatedly collapse to attack if they also occur in benign or fault-like situations.

This is a stronger final-layer preference for FDI and recurs in several common failure patterns. Because it sits at the last inference step, a high FDI probability here can directly create repeated misclassification even when upstream evidence is only partially suggestive.

This parameter is also failure-exclusive and relatively strong. Its recurrence alongside patterns with both deviation nodes selecting No suggests the model may be overcommitting to System_Fault in a specific low-deviation upstream configuration.

overall_summary: The strongest refinement candidates are Network_Manipulation and Root_Causes. Network_Manipulation has multiple failure-dominant parameters with little success overlap, indicating a plausible upstream bias toward inferring manipulation from packet-pattern evidence. Root_Causes has repeated failure-associated final-label selections across multiple columns, especially toward FDI and one System_Fault column, suggesting independent decision-boundary problems at the diagnosis layer. Other candidate CPTs are not included because their suspicious behavior is weaker, has substantial success overlap, or is better explained as downstream propagation from these more plausible contributors.
